title: Max Depth
statement: Implement `solve(value)`. A non-list has depth 0. A list's depth is 1 plus the maximum depth of its children. An empty list has depth 1. Return that integer.
hints: If the value is not a list, return 0.
If the list is empty, return 1.
Otherwise return 1 plus the max child depth.

approaches.name: Direct
approaches.explanation: Depth counts list layers, not integers.

editorial: Depth counts list layers, not integers. An integer is a leaf at depth 0, so a list of integers has depth 1. An empty list is still a list, so it has depth 1 and no children to take a max over. Forgetting the empty case and calling max() on no children throws.
